questions.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
questions.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{12}$ equal to zero.*
questions.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ -5 & 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}7 & -5 \\ -5 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(49-25) \\  & =48.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot -3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =9(30+6) \\  & =324.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & -8 & -1 \\ -3 & 3 & 7 & 5 \\ -4 & -1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{12}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
questions.worked_solution:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & -8 & -1 \\ -3 & 3 & 7 & 5 \\ -4 & -1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & 0 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & 0 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot -5\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(-8+35) \\  & =135.\end{aligned}
$$
